Appendix.title: Projection rejection and scalar components
Appendix.Content: Projection rejection and scalar components
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: Phase6
Definition and mechanism

Projection onto a nonzero axis is the along-axis vector whose remainder is orthogonal. Rejection is the remainder. Signed scalar projection measures length; the projection coefficient multiplies the target axis and need not equal that length.

For input <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> and target <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, coefficient is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>1.5</mn> </math>, scalar projection <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>3</mn> </math>, projection <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> and rejection <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>.

Appendix.title: QR factorization and least squares
Appendix.Content: QR factorization and least squares

QR writes <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>Q</mi> <mi>R</mi> </math> with orthonormal columns in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>Q</mi> </math> and triangular <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>R</mi> </math>. Orthogonal coordinates preserve Euclidean lengths, so least squares reduces to a triangular solve and a perpendicular residual. Householder QR is a stable dense method; Gram–Schmidt explains the geometry but can lose orthogonality.
Use it when: fitting overdetermined data with known full column rank.

Developed in Phase 8: Orthogonal transformations change coordinates without changing Euclidean lengths. QR therefore separates the fitted component, solved through triangular <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>R</mi> </math>, from the constant perpendicular residual; the Householder construction is the stable dense route, with Gram–Schmidt retained to make the geometry visible. Householder and Givens construction · least squares and its residual

Appendix.title: Random variables and probability laws
Appendix.Content: Random variables and probability laws
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

A random variable is a measurable mapping from outcomes to numerical values; its probability law describes how those values are distributed. Discrete laws assign probability mass to points, while continuous laws use densities relative to a chosen measure. A cumulative distribution function exists for either kind and records probability accumulated up to a threshold. Mixed distributions can contain both atoms and continuous parts. Density is not probability at an exact point, and it changes with coordinates according to a Jacobian. Expectation integrates a function against the law, whether the variable is represented by a PMF or PDF. These distinctions matter in sampling APIs: returned value, support, endpoint behavior, and reported density must refer to the same measure. A finite computer sampler approximates a continuous law with finitely many representable outputs.

Appendix.title: Ray differentials and camera sampling measures
Appendix.source: Concepts/Ray differentials and camera sampling measures.md
Appendix.Content: Ray differentials and camera sampling measures
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 11
Definition and mechanism

A camera sample selects a film location and usually a shutter time, then maps that sample to a weighted ray or path contribution. Ray differentials approximate how neighboring pixel samples change the generated ray; after intersection they estimate the surface footprint covered by a pixel and help choose a texture filter level. A sampling measure states which quantity is sampled and therefore which probability density belongs in a Monte Carlo estimator; area, solid angle, image-plane area, and discrete pixel measures are not interchangeable without a Jacobian. Example: two adjacent pixels generate rays whose intersection points span a large patch on a distant oblique surface, so filtering should average that footprint rather than use a single high-frequency texel. Differential rays are local first-order approximations and can fail at discontinuities or complex lens mappings; the weight and PDF must match the camera model and chosen measure.

Example: For a pinhole camera, offset the raster sample by one pixel in x and y, generate neighboring rays, and intersect them with a textured plane; the resulting parallelogram estimates the pixel footprint for texture filtering.

Assumptions: Differentials approximate nearby rays locally and are not exact at visibility or lens discontinuities.; Importance weights/PDFs are valid only when defined in the same measure as the estimator.

Appendix.title: Reflection refraction and shading directions
Appendix.Content: Reflection refraction and shading directions
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: University courses
Definition and mechanism

Plane reflection reverses a direction’s normal component. Refraction scales its tangent component by the incident/transmitted index ratio and solves for a unit normal component. A negative computed discriminant indicates total internal reflection under the stated model. Half-vectors require normalized outward light/view directions.

Incident <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0.6</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mn>0.8</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> reflects to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0.6</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0.8</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> across normal <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Antiparallel light/view directions have no unique half-vector.

Extend the existing direction note by separating geometric surface orientation from optical ray behavior. The normal vector is perpendicular to a local tangent plane; it determines the cosine term in diffuse shading and the directions of ideal reflection and refraction. For unit incident direction <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>ω</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> </math> and unit normal <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>n</mi> </math>, specular reflection mirrors the direction about the normal, while refraction changes direction according to the ratio of refractive indices and may undergo total internal reflection. Direction conventions matter: some texts define incoming vectors toward the surface, others point away from it, so signs must be checked before applying formulas. A shading normal may differ from the true geometric normal, as in normal mapping, but it cannot change silhouette or visibility. Distinguish shading perturbations from geometry displacement, and use consistent normals when evaluating BRDFs, ray offsets, and medium transitions.

Appendix.title: Reproducible numerical benchmarking
Appendix.Content: Reproducible numerical benchmarking
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

A useful numerical benchmark separates sample-level variability from run-level variability and pairs competing methods on the same inputs or seeds. Record the algorithm, precision, compiler/runtime settings, sample count, seed or keyed input, warm-up policy, timing method, and error metric. Compare distributions or paired differences rather than a single favorable run. A speed improvement is meaningful only if accuracy and failure rates remain acceptable for the target workload. For Monte Carlo methods, repeat independent runs and report uncertainty; for deterministic solvers, use analytical or manufactured solutions and measure convergence. Reproducibility is an experimental contract, not merely a fixed random seed. If the workload is stochastic, compare paired seeds and report both runtime and error distributions.

Appendix.title: Robust geometric predicates
Appendix.Content: Robust geometric predicates
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: Phase6
Definition and mechanism

A geometric predicate decides a category from a sign, such as orientation. Near cancellation, ordinary floating arithmetic may not certify that sign. Adaptive arithmetic adds work only when justified error bounds leave uncertainty. Exact stored-input decisions cannot restore rounded-away physical information.
A triangle can have an accurately small area estimate yet an uncertified orientation sign. Declaring every small value zero changes topology instead of proving a decision.

Adaptive orientation and incircle predicates protect discrete sign decisions from floating-point error by refining arithmetic when an error bound cannot certify the result. Camera estimation has a different uncertainty: noisy pixels and weak observability can leave pose uncertain even when every sign is exact. Predicate robustness does not improve measurement accuracy, and a low reprojection residual does not guarantee every combinatorial decision was reliable. Keep layers distinct: use robust predicates for topology, uncertainty weights for image residuals, and Jacobian spectra for weak directions. Appendix.title: Robust summaries and error metrics
Appendix.Content: Robust summaries and error metrics
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

Histograms, quantiles, medians, and robust scales summarize different features of a finite dataset. Histogram bar area represents probability only when heights are divided by sample count and bin width. Quantile conventions differ across software, so report the interpolation rule. The median minimizes absolute deviation and resists some extreme observations; the mean minimizes squared deviation and is more sensitive to outliers. MAD and trimmed means provide other robustness choices with efficiency tradeoffs. MSE and RMSE emphasize large errors, MAE is less sensitive to them, and relative metrics can become unstable near zero. Aggregating per-scene scores differs from pooling every observation. Choose the metric from the scientific question, units, and failure cost, and report tail behavior when rare large errors matter.

Definition and mechanism

The unsigned angle uses nonzero finite directions. An atan2 expression combines cross magnitude and dot, retaining sine- and cosine-like information. Scale inputs before evaluating to reduce range failures. A signed angle requires a specified oriented plane.

Parallel directions give zero, antiparallel directions give <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>π</mi> </math>, and perpendicular directions give <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>π</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> </math>. Zero input has no angle.

Appendix.title: Sampling quality: stratification, quasi-Monte Carlo, and blue noise
Appendix.source: Concepts/Sampling quality: stratification, quasi-Monte Carlo, and blue noise.md
Appendix.Content: Sampling quality: stratification, quasi-Monte Carlo, and blue noise
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

Sampling quality concerns the arrangement of points across dimensions used by an estimator, not only each coordinate’s one-dimensional histogram. Stratification partitions a domain and allocates points across cells, reducing large gaps for suitable integrands. Quasi-Monte Carlo sequences such as Sobol aim for low discrepancy and often improve integration of smooth, structured functions, though their samples are dependent and error estimates differ from IID Monte Carlo. Blue-noise point sets suppress low-frequency clumping while retaining local separation; they are useful in image sampling and spatial placement but do not automatically minimize every integral’s variance. Scrambling, domain mapping, dimensional ordering, and discontinuities affect performance. Compare methods against a clear target function and measure. The supplied probability narrative introduces stratification and Sobol but not blue-noise constructions; that part is an explicit teaching addition, not a received source claim.

Appendix.title: Scalars fields and real-number models
Appendix.Content: Scalars fields and real-number models
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: Phase6
Definition and mechanism

A scalar is an element of the field used by a vector space. A field supports addition, multiplication and nonzero division under specified algebraic laws. The reals also supply order and completeness. Floating-point values approximate this model but do not form a mathematical field.

An integer reciprocal need not be an integer; <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mn>2</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>−</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msup> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> </math>. A real scalar can carry metres or seconds. A finite representation cannot preserve every real-number operation.

Appendix.title: Screen-space ray generation and mouse picking
Appendix.source: Concepts/Screen-space ray generation and mouse picking.md
Appendix.Content: Screen-space ray generation and mouse picking
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 11 · Latest development: Phase 11
Definition and mechanism

A screen ray begins with a pixel location mapped through the viewport to NDC, then through inverse projection and camera pose into a world-space origin and direction. For perspective cameras, rays usually share the eye origin; orthographic rays have parallel directions but different origins across the image. Mouse picking must use the same high-DPI scaling, viewport offset, origin, and Y convention as rendering. Near and far unprojection can define a ray segment, but a point at infinity or an infinite far plane needs an explicit direction construction. Picking then intersects that ray with scene geometry or uses an object-ID buffer.

Appendix.title: Singular value decomposition
Appendix.Content: Singular value decomposition

For any real rectangular matrix, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>U</mi> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> <msup> <mi>V</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">T</mi> </mrow> </msup> </math>. Right singular vectors are input directions, left singular vectors are output directions, and nonnegative singular values are principal stretches. Unlike eigenvectors, the two sets live in different spaces.
Use it when: revealing rank and conditioning, solving rank-uncertain least squares, compressing a matrix, or understanding PCA.

Developed in Phase 8: The SVD expresses a rectangular map using orthonormal input and output directions joined by nonnegative stretches. Full, thin, and compact shapes have different dimensions; bidiagonal reduction and Jacobi methods compute the factors, and reconstruction, orthogonality, and triplet residuals check them independently. factor shapes · SVD algorithms and validation
Prerequisites
Matrix multiplication and composition order, Eigenvalues and eigenspaces, Dot products and orthogonality.
Used by
Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, PCA and covariance eigensystems, Polar decomposition, Matrix factorization choices.

Teaching path: SVD geometry. - Matrix norms and numerical error — Extends this foundation into the Phase 8 dependency spine. - Camera calibration and bundle adjustment - Constrained optimization and inverse kinematics
University course development

Extend the existing factorization note with its role in estimation, conditioning, and geometry. For matrix <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> </math>, the decomposition <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>U</mi> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> <msup> <mi>V</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> </math> separates orthogonal input directions, axis-aligned scaling, and orthogonal output directions. Singular values on the diagonal of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> </math> quantify how strongly each independent direction is preserved; a zero or tiny value signals rank loss or poor conditioning. Least-squares fitting can use this structure to identify which parameter combinations are well constrained and to avoid amplifying measurement noise along nearly invisible directions. The same analysis explains why a camera calibration or bundle-adjustment system can have gauge freedoms: translating or scaling the entire reconstruction may leave image measurements unchanged. Singular values diagnose these ambiguities, while constraints or fixed reference poses remove them. Thus SVD links linear algebra to robust vision, not just matrix compression.
Pose estimation, transforms, and robust fitting · Stereo, relative orientation, and reconstruction · Optimization, constraints, and inverse kinematics

Appendix.title: Sparse and iterative solvers
Appendix.Content: Sparse and iterative solvers

Sparse storage avoids zeros when structure and scale justify its index overhead. Iterative methods replace a dense factorization with matrix-vector products and a convergence process. Conjugate gradient requires symmetric positive definiteness; preconditioning, residual criteria, and a maximum iteration count belong in the contract.
Use it when: large structured systems make dense storage or factorization impractical.

Developed in Phase 8: Sparse storage pays off when zeros and dimensions outweigh indexing overhead, while direct factorization can create fill that destroys sparsity. Iterative methods instead use matrix-vector products and stopping tests; conjugate gradient requires an SPD operator, and preconditioning, a maximum iteration count, and a true residual make convergence reviewable. storage and fill · direct versus iterative solving
Prerequisites
Linear systems and fundamental subspaces, Symmetric positive-definite matrices and Cholesky, Matrix norms and numerical error.
Used by
Matrix factorization choices, Matrix storage indexing and strides.
Teaching path: sparse and iterative methods.

Appendix.title: Stable probability normalization and log-sum-exp
Appendix.Content: Stable probability normalization and log-sum-exp
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

To normalize nonnegative weights, divide each by their sum; direct summation can overflow even when the normalized probabilities are representable. Scale by the largest weight before summing. For log weights <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>a</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> </math>, compute <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>m</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>log</mi> <mo data-mjx-texclass="NONE">⁡</mo> <munder> <mo data-mjx-texclass="OP">∑</mo> <mi>i</mi> </munder> <msup> <mi>e</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <msub> <mi>a</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> <mo>−</mo> <mi>m</mi> </mrow> </msup> </math>, where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>m</mi> <mo>=</mo> <munder> <mo data-mjx-texclass="OP" movablelimits="true">max</mo> <mi>i</mi> </munder> <msub> <mi>a</mi> <mi>i</mi> </msub> </math>. Subtracting the maximum prevents exponential overflow, and the result can be used to form softmax probabilities. This assumes at least one finite, valid weight and requires an explicit policy for all-zero, negative, NaN, or infinite inputs. Underflow of very small normalized probabilities is a separate concern from overflow; do not silently equate zero after underflow with mathematically impossible. For log weights <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>1000</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1001</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>1000</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, subtracting <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>1001</mn> </math> keeps exponentials bounded while leaving the normalized probabilities unchanged.

Appendix.title: Stable quadratic root evaluation
Appendix.Content: Stable quadratic root evaluation
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

The direct quadratic formula can lose nearly all significant digits in one root when it subtracts nearly equal values. For real coefficients with nonzero leading coefficient and a valid nonnegative discriminant, compute a signed large-magnitude numerator first: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>q</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo>−</mo> <mfrac> <mn>1</mn> <mn>2</mn> </mfrac> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>b</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>copysign</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msqrt> <msup> <mi>b</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msup> <mo>−</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mi>a</mi> <mi>c</mi> </msqrt> <mo>,</mo> <mi>b</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, then obtain roots as <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>q</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>a</mi> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>c</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>q</mi> </math>. The second root follows from the product relation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mn>1</mn> </msub> <msub> <mi>x</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mi>c</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>a</mi> </math>. This avoids cancellation in the small root, but it does not prevent overflow in the discriminant or cover degenerate coefficients, nonfinite inputs, or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>q</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math>; a robust solver also scales inputs and handles those cases explicitly. For example, the small root of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>x</mi> <mn>2</mn> </msup> <mo>+</mo> <msup> <mn>10</mn> <mn>8</mn> </msup> <mi>x</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mn>1</mn> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math> is near <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo>−</mo> <msup> <mn>10</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>−</mo> <mn>8</mn> </mrow> </msup> </math>, exactly the root most endangered by direct subtraction.

Appendix.title: Stateful pseudorandom generators and stream state
Appendix.source: Concepts/Stateful pseudorandom generators and stream state.md
Appendix.Content: Stateful pseudorandom generators and stream state
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

A pseudorandom-number generator is a deterministic state transition plus an output rule. With a fixed engine, seed, and call order, its integer sequence is reproducible; it is not a source of mathematical independence by itself. Linear congruential generators are compact but have lattice and low-bit structure that can make multidimensional samples poor. Larger-state engines trade memory for period and other statistical properties. Parallel programs need an explicit stream strategy: shared state couples samples to thread scheduling, while copied seeds can duplicate streams. Reproducibility requires recording algorithm version, state, seed derivation, distribution mapping, and sampling order. Standard-library distributions may not yield identical transformed sequences across implementations. Simulation generators are not cryptographically secure unless specifically designed for that purpose.

Appendix.title: Stateless keyed sampling and reproducibility
Appendix.Content: Stateless keyed sampling and reproducibility
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

Stateless sampling derives an output from explicit coordinates such as a master seed, pixel, sample index, and dimension. The same key can be recomputed without replaying prior generator calls, which makes debugging and parallel scheduling easier. A hash mixer can provide deterministic, well-dispersed values, but reproducibility does not prove IID behavior or statistical quality. Counter-based generators use designed mixing rounds and can provide stronger parallel-stream properties under their analyzed models. Distinct sampling dimensions reduce accidental reuse, yet a dimension map must remain stable when code changes. Record the key layout, algorithm, version, and conversion to floating point. Test multidimensional patterns and estimator convergence; a good one-dimensional histogram does not establish good joint behavior.

Tangents span local surface movement; normals measure perpendicularity; bitangents supply the second tangent axis. Texture derivatives carry physical stretch. Cleaned TBN frames need normalization, degeneracy checks and a mirrored-UV sign convention.

A collapsed UV determinant cannot uniquely determine texture directions.

Appendix.title: Symmetric positive-definite matrices and Cholesky
Appendix.Content: Symmetric positive-definite matrices and Cholesky

A real symmetric matrix <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> </math> is positive definite if every nonzero <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>x</mi> </math> has positive quadratic energy <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>x</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">T</mi> </mrow> </msup> <mi>A</mi> <mi>x</mi> </math>. Then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>L</mi> <msup> <mi>L</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">T</mi> </mrow> </msup> </math> with nonsingular triangular <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>L</mi> </math>. Positive semidefinite permits zero energy directions and may be singular, so Cholesky’s assumptions and failure status must be respected.
Use it when: covariance, Gram systems, energy minimization, or an SPD solve is established.

Developed in Phase 8: Positive definiteness means every nonzero direction has positive quadratic energy, which permits a Cholesky factor and stable triangular solves. The continuation derives the positive pivots, then broadens to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>L</mi> <mi>D</mi> <msup> <mi>L</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">T</mi> </mrow> </msup> </math> when a symmetric matrix is indefinite and explains how a failed pivot reflects the assumptions or numerical scale. Appendix.title: Taylor models and approximation error
Appendix.Content: Taylor models and approximation error
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9
Definition and mechanism

A Taylor model approximates a smooth function near a reference point using its value, derivatives, and higher-order terms. The first-order model is the derivative’s linear map; the second-order model adds curvature through the Hessian. A remainder term describes what the finite truncation omits, so local accuracy depends on step size and higher derivatives over the region. Big-O notation gives an asymptotic scale, while a concrete error bound needs assumptions such as bounded derivatives. Taylor models power local optimization, camera Jacobian updates, uncertainty propagation, and numerical error analysis. They are not reliable far from the expansion point merely because the polynomial is easy to evaluate. When the input distribution is broad or crosses a singularity, first-order covariance propagation can miss bias and tail behavior; validate or replace the local model.

Appendix.title: Tensor-product interpolation
Appendix.Content: Tensor-product interpolation
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

Bilinear and trilinear interpolation apply one-dimensional linear weights independently along each coordinate axis. In a rectangular cell, each corner contributes the product of its axis weights; the weights are nonnegative and sum to one for coordinates inside the cell. This preserves the range of scalar corner values, but the interpolated surface can be twisted rather than planar, and derivatives may jump across cell boundaries. For a voxel field, trilinear interpolation provides a continuous in-cell estimate; differentiating it yields a local gradient, which need not have unit length even when samples approximate signed distance. Keep coordinates normalized to the cell and define behavior outside the sampled grid explicitly.

Appendix.title: Time integrators and symplectic updates
Appendix.Content: Time integrators and symplectic updates
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 9 · Latest development: Phase 9
Definition and mechanism

A time integrator turns a differential equation into a discrete state update. Explicit Euler uses the current slope; midpoint and Runge–Kutta methods combine several slope evaluations to improve local accuracy; semi-implicit Euler updates velocity before position and can behave better for mechanical systems. Symplectic methods preserve the geometric structure of Hamiltonian dynamics, often keeping long-run energy error bounded rather than allowing systematic drift. No method is universally best: order, stability region, cost, conservation, and stiffness all matter. A higher formal order does not guarantee better behavior at an unsuitable step size or under discontinuous forces. Compare integrators on the same problem, step policy, and error target. Update order is part of the algorithm: changing it can change stability and physical behavior, not merely code style.

Appendix.title: Triple products and signed volume
Appendix.Content: Triple products and signed volume
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: Phase6
Definition and mechanism

A scalar triple product measures oriented parallelepiped volume. Four-point orientation uses edge differences; tetrahedral volume is one sixth of the absolute result. A vector triple product is a different, vector-valued identity, and cross products are not associative.

The panel with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>D</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> has signed volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>24</mn> </math> and tetrahedron volume <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>4</mn> </math>. Parenthesis changes can turn a nested cross from a nonzero vector into zero.

Appendix.title: Uniform shuffling without replacement
Appendix.Content: Uniform shuffling without replacement
Curriculum depth: Developed · First seen: Phase 10 · Latest development: Phase 10
Definition and mechanism

Fisher–Yates generates a uniform permutation by walking from the last array element downward and choosing an index uniformly from the unshuffled prefix. Each permutation has probability <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>1</mn> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mi>n</mi> <mo>!</mo> </math> if every bounded integer choice is unbiased and the random source meets its assumptions. A common error is to use a random integer routine with modulo bias; another is to draw from the wrong interval and omit permutations. For a fixed input array, test that the output contains every original element once; statistical tests can supplement, but not replace, deterministic checks of bounds and uniqueness. The same primitive supports uniform sample subsets and randomized stratification.

Appendix.title: Unit directions and safe normalization
Appendix.Content: Unit directions and safe normalization
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: Phase6
Definition and mechanism

A unit direction is finite, nonzero input scaled to approximate length one. Scale by the largest absolute component before measuring to avoid unnecessary squared overflow or underflow. Zero has no direction; application noise thresholds are distinct from numerical existence.

For finite nonzero input, scaled squared length lies between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>1</mn> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>3</mn> </math>. A vector of huge components can have a computable unit direction even when its original length does not fit.

Appendix.title: Vector spaces subspaces and span
Appendix.Content: Vector spaces subspaces and span
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: Phase6
Definition and mechanism

A vector space is closed under addition and field-scalar multiplication with coherent algebraic laws. A subspace retains these operations inside a larger space. The span of generators is every finite linear combination of them.

The plane <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>z</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math> is a subspace of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="double-struck">R</mi> </mrow> <mn>3</mn> </msup> </math>; <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>z</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </math> is an affine translate, not a subspace. The span of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>3</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> contains all in-plane movements.

Appendix.title: Vector storage SIMD and boundary layouts
Appendix.source: Concepts/Vector storage SIMD and boundary layouts.md
Appendix.Content: Vector storage SIMD and boundary layouts
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: Phase6
Definition and mechanism

Storage layout, compute lanes and external buffer layout are separate contracts. SIMD may operate within one vector or across objects. AoS, SoA and AoSoA change access patterns. Alignment and padding must be measured; a spare lane is not implicitly valid homogeneous data.
One million twelve-byte vectors occupy four million fewer payload bytes than sixteen-byte vectors. A sixteen-byte load still needs sixteen accessible bytes even if one lane is discarded.

Appendix.title: Vector tolerances and finite-state diagnostics
Appendix.Content: Vector tolerances and finite-state diagnostics
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: Phase6
Definition and mechanism

Closeness depends on a declared distance or angular criterion. Combined absolute/relative scalar rules differ from component boxes and Euclidean balls. NaN/infinity policies are explicit. Diagnose the first invalid stage rather than only the final visible symptom.

Errors <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0.09</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0.09</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> pass component tolerance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>0.1</mn> </math> but fail Euclidean tolerance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>0.1</mn> </math>. Near <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mn>10</mn> <mn>8</mn> </msup> </math>, binary32 can lose a one-unit displacement at storage.

Appendix.title: Vector value types and component access
Appendix.source: Concepts/Vector value types and component access.md
Appendix.Content: Vector value types and component access
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: Phase6
Definition and mechanism

A vector value type stores components directly with coherent arithmetic and initialization. Named members are not an array. Named dot, cross and Hadamard operations avoid ambiguous vector multiplication; writable swizzles need explicit alias policies.
A checked component accessor selects one of three real members and rejects out-of-range indices. It does not traverse from the address of the first member.

Appendix.title: Vectors coordinates and affine points
Appendix.Content: Vectors coordinates and affine points
Curriculum depth: Introduced · First seen: Phase6 · Latest development: Phase6
Definition and mechanism

A free vector describes movement independently of its starting point. A coordinate tuple describes that vector relative to an ordered basis. An affine point is a location without an intrinsic preferred origin. Point differences produce vectors; point translations produce points.

For the workcell panel, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>B</mi> <mo>−</mo> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>4</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> is a displacement in metres. Changing the origin changes point coordinates but cancels in this difference.

Appendix.Content: M004 - Representation and rounding learning spine

Cell.Content: A 32-bit binary interchange format with one sign bit, eight exponent bits and 23 fraction bits. Normal precision is 24 bits; exponent bias is 127. Word 3F800000 has E=127,F=0 and means 1.
A 64-bit binary interchange format with 1/11/52 fields, 53 significant normal bits and bias 1023. Normal exponent range is −1022 through 1023. Word 3FF0000000000000 means 1.
Normal exponents are encoded as unsigned E=e+B. Binary32 B=127, so exponent 3 stores 130. Field zero and all-ones are reserved; classify before subtracting bias.

The significand supplies significant digits; the exponent supplies scale. A normal binary value begins 1.f, so its leading one is implied, not stored. Binary32 fraction F contributes F/2^23; subnormals instead begin 0.f.
Exponent bias, Significand and hidden bit, Hexadecimal
Encoding chooses fields for a value; decoding classifies fields and reconstructs their meaning. 10.625 normalizes to 1.010101₂×2³, giving 412A0000. C1540000 decodes to −13.25.
Exponent and fraction zero permit either sign. 00000000 and 80000000 compare numerically equal, but signbit and reciprocal distinguish them. Ordinary x<0 does not detect negative zero.
All-one exponent and zero fraction encode signed infinity. This is not maximum finite. Infinity minus itself is NaN; overflow’s result also depends on rounding direction.

All-one exponent with nonzero fraction encodes a non-numerical, unordered NaN. Quiet and signaling classes differ; fraction bits can carry payload information. Ordinary NaN equality is false; use isnan. Raw words can be classified without consuming signaling NaNs as floating values.
Exponent bias, Significand and hidden bit

Exponent zero and nonzero fraction remove the hidden one and hold the effective exponent at the normal minimum. Binary32 values are F×2^-149, connecting smoothly to 2^-126. Absolute spacing stays fixed while relative precision degrades.
For these binary types epsilon is upward spacing at 1: 2^-23 for binary32 and 2^-52 for binary64. It is neither minimum positive value nor a physical threshold.
Machine epsilon, Exponent bias, Subnormals and gradual underflow
A unit in the last place describes local spacing. Inside normal binade [2e,2(e+1)), p-bit precision gives spacing 2^(e-(p-1)). Immediately above 1 the binary32 gap is twice the gap below it.

Content.Link: Rounding to nearest ties to even

Cell.Content: Choose the nearest representable value; exactly halfway choose the even retained significand integer. At toy precision three bits, 1.125→1 and 1.375→1.5. std::round uses halfway-away-from-zero instead.
ULP and representable spacing, Rounding to nearest ties to even
Under nearest binary rounding the conventional relative bound for normal-range results is u=2^-p, half upward epsilon. For binary32 this is 2^-24. The bound has range/rounding assumptions.
Boolean algebra, Rounding to nearest ties to even
Guard is first discarded bit, round the next, sticky ORs all remaining bits. With retained low bit L, nearest-even increments when G AND (R OR sticky OR L). Sticky summarizes any nonzero tail.

Content.Link: Rounding to nearest ties to even

Cell.Content: Upward means toward positive infinity, downward toward negative infinity, and toward-zero truncates magnitude. Upward rounding of −2.1 to an integer gives −2, not −3.
Directed rounding modes, NaNs and payloads

The environment includes rounding direction and exception status. Runtime mode changes can fail and must restore prior state. Strict compiler settings are needed; fast-math may discard required special-value or environment assumptions.
IEEE-754 floating point, Subnormals and gradual underflow

Invalid, divide-by-zero, overflow, underflow and inexact are status conditions, not C++ throw exceptions. Exact subnormal results need not signal underflow. Flag/trap behavior depends on the environment.
Subnormals and gradual underflow, Floating-point environment and compiler modes
FTZ flushes certain tiny results to zero; DAZ treats subnormal inputs as zero in supporting environments. They change gradual-underflow behavior. Cost and support are target/mode-specific.
Fixed-width integer types, Interpretation contract, IEEE-754 floating point

A same-size eligible bit_cast transfers representation, not numeric value. On the checked binary32 host, bit_cast<uint32_t>(1.0f)=3F800000, whereas a numeric cast gives 1. Pointer punning is not an equivalent legal operation.
ULP and representable spacing, Signed zero, NaNs and payloads

Distance counts representable steps under a declared ordering/equality policy. The finite-only laboratory collapses both zeros to one key and rejects NaNs/infinities. Across negative minimum subnormal to positive minimum subnormal distance is two.
Machine epsilon, ULP and representable spacing, Floating-point infinities, NaNs and payloads

Tolerance is a task-chosen allowed discrepancy: absolute in original units, relative to scale, or representable-step based. Machine epsilon is not automatically a norm cutoff. Handle non-finite values and validate tolerances before formulas.

A final representable answer can be lost to overflowing intermediates. Squaring 1e20f overflows before a finite norm could be formed. Scale by maximum component or use hypot to avoid unnecessary squared overflow.

Conditioning measures sensitivity to input perturbation. A=1e-4 I has determinant 1e-8 but condition number one in the 2-norm. Uniform scaling changes determinant magnitude without changing this conditioning measure.
Signed zero, NaNs and payloads, Serialization, Bit casting and representation

Canonicalization deliberately merges encodings: both zeros to positive zero, all NaNs to one quiet pattern. Raw preservation instead keeps sign/payload distinctions. Neither is universally correct; this is a file/hash contract choice.
Directed rounding modes, Floating-point environment and compiler modes
An interval encloses a possible exact value between lower and upper bounds. Correct outward rounding can preserve containment when the whole algorithm honors necessary assumptions.

Appendix.Content: Representation choices and external contracts

Cell.Content: A raw integer I represents I/S for an agreed positive scale S and units. With S=2^16, raw 212992 means 3.25. The integer has no built-in fractional point.
For signed N-bit raw storage and F fraction bits, step is 2^-F and the positive endpoint is (2(N-1)-1)/2F. Required step 0.001 and magnitude 1e6 in 32 bits allow F=10 or 11.
Fixed-point representation, Minimum signed value, Arithmetic policies

Raw multiplication changes scale S to S²; divide the wide product by S with a declared rounding rule. Raw division uses A*S/B. Check the destination after widening, and handle divisor zero and signed minima.
Fixed-point representation, Absolute and relative error
A positive step s, integer zero point z and bounded code q reconstruct x̂=s(q-z). Nearest encode uses clamp(round(x/s)+z). Half-step error assumes no clipping and ideal parameters.
Affine quantization and zero point, Bit packing
Local groups share a scale, improving adaptation at a metadata cost. Symmetric INT4 calibration maxAbs/7 reconstructs codes around [-7,7]; float scales add about 32/G bits per value for full groups.
One sign label selects one of two row means. Row [-1,-3,2,4] reconstructs [-2,-2,3,3], with RMSE one. Two float32 centroids cost 64 additional bits per row.
UNORM decodes q/(2^n-1); UNORM8 code128 gives128/255. SNORM commonly clamps q/(2^(n-1)-1) at -1, so -128 and -127 both map to -1 for eight bits.
IEEE-754 floating point, Rounding to nearest ties to even
IEEE binary16 has 1/5/10 fields, bias15 and11 normal precision bits. Word3E00 is1.5; maximum finite65504; normal minimum2^-14 and subnormal minimum2^-24.
IEEE-754 floating point, Rounding to nearest ties to even
BF16 has1/8/7 fields, bias127 and8 normal precision bits. It keeps broad exponent range at coarse spacing2^-7 above1. A nearest-even conversion must handle NaNs separately from finite rounding.
A bias turns signed levels into unsigned codes. For the source-shaped INT4 convention c=q+8, -3 becomes nibble0101, not the two’s-complement nibble1101.
Absolute and relative error, Quantization and compressed weights

For N>0, RMSE is sqrt(sum squared discrepancies/N), MAE is mean absolute discrepancy, and max error is the largest observed magnitude. Promote float operands before subtraction when measuring in double.

A schema declares field widths/order, byte order, numeric representation, valid values, lengths, version, padding and identity policy. Magic identifies a candidate format; version chooses a schema, neither authenticates content.
Binary format contracts, Unsigned modular arithmetic, Short-circuit evaluation

Validate products before size calculation, ranges with offset≤size and length≤size-offset, and practical resource limits before allocation. Mapping/alignment does not itself establish valid typed object access.

Checksums/digests summarize specified bytes. Additive checksums miss reorderings; CRCs use GF(2) polynomial remainders and declared parameters. Cryptographic hashes need a trusted reference to support integrity claims against substitution.
Checksums CRCs and hashes, Interpretation contract
Integrity compares content with a declared reference; authenticity requires a trust mechanism such as a MAC or signature. Replacing both file and untrusted digest defeats a simple hash comparison.
Endianness, Bit casting and representation, Binary format contracts

Raw octets gain meaning from offsets, width, encoding and byte order. Bytes00 00 80 3F mean integer1065353216 or binary32 one under different little-endian contracts. A dump does not prove a typed object is live.

Incorrect animation and platform-testing claims were rejected; historical announcements are retained as catalog/roadmap evidence, not implemented features. Animation workflow, method inputs/composition order, packaging dependencies and API capability contracts were developed in the engine/foundations books. At that historical checkpoint, totals were 14,240 reviewed and 15,475 pending; the current table above supersedes those figures. This is still an unfinished whole-corpus review. Exact source/point decisions.
Current repair and retention boundary — 14 November 2026

The supervised repair record separates implemented teaching, executed checks, unresolved source review and cleanup. Source captions and acquisition scripts have not been retired: the 1,230 pending claim texts and 103 open extraction jobs require their retained evidence. This local repair does not resume acquisition or mark unread book pages complete.

A phase can hold different levels for different claims. For example, Vulkan synchronization can have a native API smoke witness while transient aliasing remains only derived. Do not average those into one misleading score.

Appendix.Content: What this repair changed
The repair specifically closes the former representation gap where a topic could be called developed because a heading or short concept card existed. The repository now has:

ListItem.Content: no Concepts/*.md file below the structural 1200-byte smoke floor;
explicit evidence levels rather than one ambiguous developed state;
an expanded family of independently compiled/run C++ reference laboratories for the previously weakest subjects;
native Vulkan synchronization2/resource/image execution CI and Metal shader compilation plus command-buffer compute execution CI;
reconstruction checkpoints inside all three canonical master volumes;
known-answer cryptographic tests rather than prose-only primitive names;
real POSIX loopback and mmap/descriptor execution;
Phase 29 tensor/GGUF/ONNX/quantized-attention runtime ownership instead of an effectively blank phase;
Phase 30 host-neutral publication/DCC boundaries instead of tool-name mentions;
independent raster, PBR, Monte Carlo, Gaussian, temporal-rendering, ECS, spatial and mesh/skinning oracles.

Appendix.Content: Why remaining boundaries are recorded rather than hidden
The goal is maximum depth, not maximum confidence language. Some proof layers require hardware, external applications, current production repositories or human reconstruction:

ListItem.Content: a software Vulkan ICD now proves API execution/validation for synchronization, buffer visibility/timeline, and image-layout/readback contracts, but not discrete-vendor physical-GPU performance;
the current macOS CI host executed a real Metal compute pipeline, but heap aliasing, explicit hazard-tracking captures, render-pass behavior, multi-queue synchronization and production parity remain;
a CPU Gaussian oracle can expose projection bugs but does not certify the current Maveb Metal kernel;
an educational SHA/HMAC/HKDF implementation can prove bit-level understanding and known-answer agreement but should not become production cryptography;
Blender now has a real headless host round trip; Maya/Houdini/Nuke remain host-neutral until equivalent licensed/current hosts execute their adapters;
written material cannot prove Level 7 reconstructed mastery until a learner derives/implements/debugs it without copying.

Appendix.Content: Those are not excuses or hidden gaps. They are the next evidence layer attached to the exact claim that needs it.
Regression gates
tools/check_depth_repair_contract.py checks that:

ListItem.Content: every required repair artifact still exists;
no concept card silently collapses below the 1200-byte structural floor;
exactly the three canonical continuous volumes remain;
each canonical volume retains its reconstruction checkpoints.

Appendix.Content: The generic C++20 workflow separately compiles and executes every tools/labs/*_lab.cpp under GCC sanitizer, Clang strict and GCC release modes. The native graphics workflow exercises Vulkan and Metal-specific toolchains. The consolidation/source-sync workflows protect the three-volume teaching surface.
These checks are necessary evidence, not a semantic completion certificate.
Second-wave closure — executable boundaries tightened
The follow-up repair converted four previously explicit boundaries into tested reference artifacts:

ListItem.Content: ecs_scheduler_hierarchy_lab.cpp adds read/write conflict scheduling and subtree transform invalidation to the ECS layer;
path_transport_scene_lab.cpp connects camera geometry, Lambertian transport, two proposal PDFs and balance MIS to an analytic pixel target;
gaussian_tile_conic_lab.cpp continues projected covariance through conic inversion, conservative tile duplication, depth ordering and transmittance;
qem_edge_collapse_lab.cpp moves mesh simplification from topology-only discussion to plane quadrics, candidate error and geometric collapse rejection.

Appendix.Content: These raise the corresponding claims from prose/partial-reference status. They do not erase the higher evidence boundaries stated in the phase table.
Third-wave closure — pipeline state, spatial quality, solver coupling, and model containers
The next repair wave closes another set of previously explicit reference gaps without promoting them beyond the evidence actually executed:

ListItem.Content: raster_pipeline_state_lab.cpp extends raster semantics through homogeneous clipping, explicit multisample coverage, stencil state, and premultiplied blending;
pbr_extended_reference_lab.cpp adds anisotropic GGX normalization, exact dielectric Fresnel, Snell refraction/total internal reflection, and a white-furnace energy integral;
bvh_sah_refit_lab.cpp adds surface-area split reasoning, Morton interleaving, and parent-bound refit to the earlier BVH query oracle;
constraint_friction_island_lab.cpp adds island connectivity, unilateral impulses, Coulomb friction clamping, and a tiny sequential-impulse stack;
gguf_metadata_tensor_lab.cpp advances GGUF from prefix-only validation to typed metadata, alignment and tensor descriptors.

Appendix.Content: These are reference-level closures. Exact hardware/API behavior, production repository parity, third-party DCC execution, and learner Level-7 reconstruction are still tracked separately rather than absorbed into a generic “complete” label.
Native execution escalation

The native graphics gate now goes beyond syntax-level API examples. Vulkan executes a real transfer fill into an allocated/bound buffer, records a resource-specific synchronization2 buffer barrier from transfer-write to host-read, signals a timeline semaphore, waits for a concrete timeline value, maps the memory and checks the written pattern. Metal compiles the MSL kernel and, when the macOS CI host exposes a Metal device, loads the metallib, creates a compute pipeline/queue/shared buffers, dispatches work, waits for command completion and validates the result. On the current macOS-15 CI run the host exposed a Metal device and the runtime witness passed; the SKIP path remains only as an honest fallback for future hosts without a device.

This still does not elevate every Phase 23/24 claim to native verification. Image layout transitions, queue-family ownership, descriptor/shader visibility, heap aliasing, multi-queue behavior, capture-derived hazard evidence, and current Kairo/Maveb integration remain individually gated.
DCC execution escalation

Blender is no longer represented only by prose or a host-neutral adapter. The dedicated CI workflow launches Blender in background mode, constructs a deterministic mesh asset and collection through bpy, attaches logical publication metadata, saves the source .blend, exports GLB, validates the GLB container/JSON contract, resets the host, re-imports the published artifact and checks geometry plus custom identity fields.

This is intentionally a Blender-only native-host escalation. Maya, Houdini and Nuke are not marked executed because their current hosts/licenses are not available in this CI environment. Their contracts remain explicit and can be promoted only when equivalent host-side witnesses exist.
Fourth-wave closure — temporal effects, native image state, security, and host DCC
The latest repair wave closes four more areas that were previously recorded only as future boundaries.

Advanced real-time effects. realtime_effects_reference_lab.cpp now checks deterministic Halton jitter, current-neighborhood history clipping, a screen-space depth-crossing ray-march oracle, SSAO-style depth/thickness visibility, homogeneous Beer–Lambert transmittance, and deterministic particle update/death/stable compaction. These are deliberately semantic CPU references; production Hi-Z traversal, GTAO, froxel scattering, reactive masks and native GPU particle systems remain higher evidence levels.

Vulkan images. vulkan_image_layout_smoke.cpp moves native evidence beyond a generic barrier and buffer visibility. It allocates an optimal-tiled RGBA image, records UNDEFINED → TRANSFER_DST → TRANSFER_SRC synchronization2 layout transitions, clears it, copies to a host-visible buffer, performs transfer-to-host synchronization and checks the UNORM bytes under validation. Queue-family ownership, descriptor/shader hazards and presentation remain separate.

Authenticated encryption. openssl_aes_gcm_smoke.cpp checks a standard AES-128-GCM known-answer vector through OpenSSL EVP, authenticated round trip, tag and AAD tamper rejection, nonce-sensitive output and discard-on-authentication-failure behavior. The evidence is for the primitive/API contract, not for nonce persistence, replay defense, key management or a complete production protocol.

DCC execution. Blender is now exercised as a real host rather than only named in an adapter contract: background Python creates the asset, saves the source scene, exports GLB with logical metadata, validates the binary glTF container, resets the host, re-imports the publication and checks geometry plus identity fields. Maya, Houdini and Nuke remain explicitly unexecuted rather than being promoted by analogy.
ONNX interchange escalation

Phase 29 no longer stops at a hand-modeled SSA graph contract. tools/ml/onnx_contract.py creates a real ONNX ModelProto, serializes and reloads the protobuf, preserves named initializers and opset metadata, passes the official checker, runs official symbolic shape inference, executes MatMul → Add → Relu with the ONNX reference evaluator, compares against an independently computed NumPy result, and requires the official checker to reject a duplicate-output SSA violation.

This proves a bounded interchange/runtime slice, not universal ONNX support. Control-flow subgraphs, external data, arbitrary opsets/operators, custom domains, ONNX Runtime/device lowering, quantized operator kernels and current KairoONNX parity remain separate evidence gates.

Appendix.Content: Recall test: redraw one card without looking, reproduce its arithmetic, then state a case where its formula cannot safely be used. For uncertainty in determinant signs, reopen the predicate discussion rather than adding a universal epsilon.
Whole-story overview
Caption: Coordinates describe a geometric object relative to a basis; they are not the object itself. A point has a location role; a vector has a displacement role.
Geometry operations by question

Cell.Content: Scale inputs before squaring when range could overflow/underflow.
Sign and magnitude depend on lengths; normalize only after validating nonzero finite inputs.
What part points along a direction?
Decompose into parallel and perpendicular components.
Which way is the oriented surface facing?
Order/winding matters; magnitude is parallelogram area.
Near-zero signs can be numerically uncertain.
Weights sum to one; perspective interpolation changes screen-space weights.
Convert shared-point question to whether the origin is in the difference set.

Appendix.Content: Coordinate frame: same movement, different coordinates

Caption: Changing components does not change the underlying vector. In a non-orthonormal basis, ordinary component dot products do not directly equal geometric inner products; the Gram matrix carries the metric.
Robust computation: validate before normalizing or deciding
Caption: Clamping an invalid intermediate is not a proof that the original geometry was valid. Input validity, arithmetic range, tolerance meaning and decision confidence are separate checks.
A three-number type is not the complete contract
Appendix.Code: geometric promise ──> initialization, role, units, space storage promise ──> size, alignment, offsets, stride execution promise ──> scalar/SIMD behavior and errors boundary promise ──> GPU format, shader layout, serialization
Appendix.Content: Caption: A 12-byte CPU Vec3 does not prove shader compatibility, array semantics, safe indexing, or a portable file representation.
Retrieval prompts

ListItem.Content: Why can point minus point produce a vector, but point plus point be meaningless?
What does a basis change alter, and what stays fixed?
Why does a cross-product sign depend on order and handedness?
Which exact conditions make a normalized vector meaningful?
Why does perspective correction change barycentric interpolation?
Why must the normal matrix be the inverse transpose?
What evidence distinguishes a robust predicate from a merely tested floating-point expression?

BlockQuote.Content: [!answer]- Compact key Affine points have no intrinsic origin, while displacements do. Coordinates depend on the chosen basis; the geometric vector does not. Cross product is antisymmetric and encodes orientation. A direction needs finite, nonzero input and range-safe length computation. Perspective division is nonlinear, so interpolation must account for reciprocal depth. The inverse transpose preserves tangent-normal orthogonality under a general linear transform. A tested expression is evidence over those cases; a robust/certified claim requires stated assumptions and a procedure that guarantees the decision.

Appendix.Content: Teach the full Phase 6 story · Part coverage · Derivations
One-page active-recall mini-atlas

Use each row as a prompt: say the rule, state its precondition, then point to the linked chapter section for the full explanation and figures. The short cues are retrieval hooks, not replacements for the teaching narrative.

Content.Strong: What is the robot trying to represent?

Cell.Content: A tuple is only storage; decide whether it means a point, displacement, direction, unit normal, or measurement, and state its frame and units.
Panel and problem setup · Vec3 contracts

Content.Strong: What changes when I change coordinates?

Cell.Content: The geometric vector stays fixed; its components change with the basis. A skew basis needs its Gram matrix to measure angles and lengths correctly.
Points and vectors · Basis change · Gram matrix

Content.Strong: Can the robot reach this movement?

Cell.Content: Allowed combinations form a span; closure under addition and scalar scaling makes a subspace. Independence means no control direction is redundant.

Content.Strong: How much, which way, how aligned?

Cell.Content: Norm measures length; dot measures alignment; projection extracts a component. Check finite/nonzero inputs before normalization and scale before squaring.
Norm and distance · Dot and angle · Projection

Content.Strong: Which side is the panel facing?

Cell.Content: Cross-product order encodes orientation; magnitude is area. A triple product gives signed volume; near-zero signs need a reliability policy.
Cross product and winding · Signed volume

Content.Strong: How do I make a stable local surface frame?

Cell.Content: Choose tangents, reject the unwanted component, then normalize safely. Gram–Schmidt is repeated rejection; order and precision affect the result.
Reflection flips the normal component; refraction changes the tangent component. Normals are covectors: transform them with inverse transpose to preserve perpendicularity.

Content.Strong: Where is the sensor on the triangle?

Cell.Content: Barycentric weights sum to one; they locate points and interpolate attributes. Perspective projection changes screen-space weights; orientation predicates need trustworthy signs.
Convex combinations describe convex shapes; a Minkowski difference turns intersection into asking whether the origin belongs to the difference.
Homogeneous coordinates let matrix operations express translation; projective points have equivalent scaled representatives. NDC is not a normalized direction.
Floating-point arithmetic can overflow, underflow, lose small changes, or give an uncertain sign. Validate inputs, scale safely, then apply explicit tolerance/error policy.

Content.Strong: What must the C++ type/API promise?

Cell.Content: Separate geometric role, units, scalar precision, memory layout, SIMD behavior, and GPU/serialization agreement; Vec3 alone proves none of the external contracts.
Semantic types · CPU/GPU layout · Executable reference and tests

Appendix.Content: Landscape concept maps
The panel: from geometry to engine data
Caption: Read left to right as the robot’s work, not a list of disconnected formulas. Revisit the panel setup and the sensor's triangle coordinates.
Three tools, three different questions
Caption: Do not substitute one operation for another: they answer different geometric questions. See dot, cross, and projection.
Reliability ladder
Caption: A mathematically valid construction is not automatically a reliable machine decision. Follow safe norm, predicate reliability, and calculation boundary.
Added retrieval prompt
Camera framing uses a point angle atan2(y,z); double the largest half-angle for full vertical FOV; include asin(r/d) for a sphere. Rebuild the camera trace.
M06-1. Reflection across the horizontal mirror normal. The shown incident vector has v dot n=-1 and reflected vector r=(2,1); both squared norms are 5.
Vectors as measurements — retrieve the missing steps

Cell.Content: Why do dot measurements differ from coordinates?
A slanted reconstruction basis needs reciprocal measuring directions.
[[Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#Recover a component with the right measuring rule
Is every norm an ordinary dot-product length?
No. The taxicab norm fails the parallelogram identity.
[[Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#Choose what a length is meant to measure
What does a dual norm measure?
Worst scalar response over an allowed vector-error ball.
[[Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#Bound a measurement using a dual norm
Is the Euclidean nearest point always the right constrained answer?
Only for that distance rule; a weighted ruler changes the correction direction.
[[Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#A rail, a wall, and a feasible region use the same nearest-point question
A differential measures change; a metric turns it into a gradient vector.
[[Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#A derivative measures change; a gradient needs a ruler
Can a mesh boundary be a vector?
Yes: coefficients weight elements; boundary is linear.
[[Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#The same vector rules can describe a triangle’s boundary
Only in special configurations/conventions; instantaneous axes form a state-dependent map.
[[Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#Angle rates are not three components of angular velocity

A scalar measurement has variance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>a</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="sans-serif">T</mi> </mrow> </mrow> </msup> <mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi> <mi>a</mi> </math>.
[[Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#Measure uncertainty along an actual direction
Is a unit uncertainty ellipse a 68% region?
Not generally. The stated two-dimensional Gaussian unit ellipse contains about 39.35%.
[[Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#Whiten residuals without pretending every ellipse has the same probability
How do vertex samples become a derivative?
Barycentric gradients reconstruct a constant field gradient per flat triangle.
[[Continuous Notes/Computing Foundations - From Bits to C++ and Systems APIs#A triangle turns a differential into a concrete field calculation

Appendix.Content: Matrices, Transforms and Quaternions — Visual Recall

Companion to the Phase 7 teaching story. Start with the short route, reconstruct a worked figure, then follow its link when an assumption or definition is missing. Six excerpts supply 84 numbered lessons; the affine bridge is reconstruction, and Parts 635–650 remain source gaps.
The short route

Convention card: active right-handed rotations; column vectors; <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>y</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mi>M</mi> <mi>x</mi> </math>; rightmost operation first; code angles in radians; Hamilton quaternion components <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>w</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>y</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>z</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>. Row-major storage does not choose any of those mathematical conventions.

RowValue.Content: A rectangular table becomes a map only after input/output bases and roles are fixed. Columns are input-basis images.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>m</mi> <mo>×</mo> <mi>k</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>k</mi> <mo>×</mo> <mi>n</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> yields <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>m</mi> <mo>×</mo> <mi>n</mi> </math>; shared dimensions must match. Addition needs equal shape.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mi>B</mi> <mi>x</mi> </math> applies <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>B</mi> </math> first. Noncommutative order is separate from associative grouping; floating-point regrouping can change bits.

Derive columns from rotated axes. For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>R</mi> <mi>y</mi> </msub> </math>, rotate the oriented pair <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>z</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, then restore <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>x</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>y</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>z</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> order.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>A</mi> <mi>B</mi> <msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <mo>=</mo> <msup> <mi>B</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <msup> <mi>A</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> </math>; <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>A</mi> <mo>+</mo> <msup> <mi>A</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> <mo>+</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>A</mi> <mo>−</mo> <msup> <mi>A</mi> <mi>T</mi> </msup> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> </math>. Trace is similarity-invariant, not a full map identifier.
Magnitude = volume scale; sign = orientation; zero = rank loss for square maps. It does not measure conditioning alone.
Cofactors explain a formula; pivoted elimination explains an algorithm. Solve directly when the inverse itself is unnecessary.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>κ</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>A</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mo data-mjx-texclass="ORD" fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo> <mi>A</mi> <mo data-mjx-texclass="ORD" fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo> <mo data-mjx-texclass="ORD" fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo> <msup> <mi>A</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>−</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msup> <mo data-mjx-texclass="ORD" fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo> </math> in a compatible norm. Stable code cannot restore information lost to input uncertainty.

Affine points receive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mi>p</mi> <mo>+</mo> <mi>t</mi> </math>; displacements receive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mi>v</mi> </math>. Homogeneous <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>w</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>w</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math> expose the distinction.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msubsup> <mi>F</mi> <mi>C</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>−</mo> <mn>1</mn> </mrow> </msubsup> <msub> <mi>F</mi> <mi>B</mi> </msub> </math> converts B-coordinates to C-coordinates. The camera view is the inverse camera pose.

Clip retains <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>w</mi> </math>; NDC divides by valid <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>w</mi> </math>. Clipping, depth range and backend conventions remain explicit.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>n</mi> <mo data-mjx-alternate="1">′</mo> </msup> <mo>=</mo> <msup> <mi>A</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>−</mo> <mi>T</mi> </mrow> </msup> <mi>n</mi> </math> preserves zero action on transformed tangents. Normalize only after a valid transformation.
Logical width is not physical stride. Real arrays provide array bounds; views borrow both layout and lifetime.
SIMD, loop order and tiling change reuse and rounding. Measure hardware/workload; algebra alone supplies no speedup.
Hamilton product = scalar/dot part + weighted vectors/cross part. Unit <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>q</mi> </math> permits inverse-by-conjugate.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>q</mi> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>cos</mi> <mo data-mjx-texclass="NONE">⁡</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>θ</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo>,</mo> <mi>a</mi> <mi>sin</mi> <mo data-mjx-texclass="NONE">⁡</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>θ</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math> for unit axis. Two-sided action produces the full angle; <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>q</mi> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo>−</mo> <mi>q</mi> </math> share orientation.

Quaternion↔matrix tests compare basis actions; near <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mn>180</mn> <mo>∘</mo> </msup> </math> recover a large component. Reject scale/shear/reflection as rotation inputs.
Sign-align endpoints. NLERP normalizes the chord; SLERP advances on the great circle. Small-angle fallback needs a policy.
Axis sequence is part of the type contract. Gimbal lock is a singular coordinate chart; original angle history cannot be recovered.

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mi>d</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mi>t</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mi>r</mi> </msub> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> </math>; require <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mo data-mjx-texclass="ORD" fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mi>r</mi> </msub> <mo data-mjx-texclass="ORD" fence="false" stretchy="false">‖</mo> <mo>=</mo> <mn>1</mn> </math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mi>r</mi> </msub> <mo>⋅</mo> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mi>d</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mn>0</mn> </math>. Do not normalize the two halves independently.
Local TRS is useful authoring data; full affine world products may contain shear. Dirty flags record dependency invalidation.
M10: choose representation · M11: cache dependencies

For <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mi>Z</mi> </msub> <mo>=</mo> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <msqrt> <mn>2</mn> </msqrt> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <mn>0</mn> <mo>,</mo> <msqrt> <mn>2</mn> </msqrt> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mo>/</mo> </mrow> <mn>2</mn> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>, rotate X to Y. Then use <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mn>2</mn> <msub> <mi>q</mi> <mi>Z</mi> </msub> </math>: true inverse still gives Y, conjugate sandwich gives four times Y, and the unit-optimized formula is outside its contract.

Appendix.Content: Phase 8 — Linear Algebra: Active Recall

Fast spine: Measurements constrain → rank separates knowledge from freedom → factorizations expose structure → eigenvectors describe square-map directions → SVD describes every map → stable APIs report evidence.
Read the full explanations in From Constraints to Spectra. These figure links jump to their source chapters.
The story at a glance
Retrieve the mechanisms

RowLabel.Content: Why may <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>A</mi> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="bold">x</mi> </mrow> <mo>=</mo> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="bold">b</mi> </mrow> </math> have no answer?

RowValue.Content: The target is outside <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>Col</mi> <mo stretchy="false">(</mo> <mi>A</mi> <mo stretchy="false">)</mo> </math>.

RowLabel.Content: What does a null vector mean?

RowValue.Content: An input change no measurement can see; add it to any solution.
The solution set, only if row operations also transform <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mrow data-mjx-texclass="ORD"> <mi mathvariant="bold">b</mi> </mrow> </math>.

Reuse <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>L</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>U</mi> </math> or <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <mi>Q</mi> <mo>,</mo> <mi>R</mi> </math> for additional right-hand sides.
LU general square; Cholesky SPD; QR least squares; SVD rank insight; iteration for huge sparse systems when suitable.

RowLabel.Content: What does a small residual prove?

RowValue.Content: Near satisfaction of the equations; sensitivity can still make the solution inaccurate.

RowLabel.Content: Why is a symmetric eigenbasis special?

RowValue.Content: It is orthonormal, preserving 2-norm while diagonalizing the map.
Input orthogonal coordinates → independent stretches → output orthogonal coordinates.

Exact <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msup> <mi>A</mi> <mo>+</mo> </msup> </math>: least-squares fit, then minimum norm. Truncated <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"> <msubsup> <mi>A</mi> <mi>τ</mi> <mo>+</mo> </msubsup> </math>: solve the retained-rank problem; original residual can increase.

RowLabel.Content: How does PCA connect to SVD?
